buckets.label: Workflow it
buckets.hint: Recurring transformation of material you own

tasks.text: Turning each week's interview notes into structured debriefs
tasks.reasoning: The canonical first build: weekly, structured, your notes.

tasks.text: Drafting the monthly people-metrics narrative from a data export you own
tasks.reasoning: Your export, same shape monthly; verification catches the numbers.

tasks.text: Deciding which of two finalists receives the offer
tasks.reasoning: A decision about a person. It isn't about capability, and it doesn't move for better models.

tasks.text: Refreshing job postings each quarter to strip jargon and drift
tasks.reasoning: Quarterly but perfectly structured, pure transformation.

tasks.text: Responding to an employee's grievance email
tasks.reasoning: Arrives on a rhythm, but each one is a distinct human situation carrying legal weight. AI can help you understand a policy; the response is authored, not generated.

tasks.text: Summarizing exit-interview verbatims at quarter end
tasks.reasoning: Same pattern as engagement summaries, with the same caveat: read the raw comments too.

tasks.text: Setting performance ratings ahead of calibration
tasks.reasoning: The decision where bias stops being abstract: automation reproduces patterns at scale and speed, and adverse impact is the mechanism.

tasks.text: Drafting the weekly HR newsletter from bullet points you supply
tasks.reasoning: Low stakes, weekly, you supply every bullet.
A one-off, and one of the highest-stakes documents you'll ever write. Fails the 'recurs' test before stakes even enter it.

tasks.text: Translating policy updates into plain-language change notes
Screening résumés for a hard-to-fill role
tasks.reasoning: A decision about people, and the place your vendors quietly systematize it for you. You wrote the questions to ask them in 101.

tasks.text: Preparing talking points for a sensitive conversation with a specific employee
tasks.reasoning: The material that matters (history, relationship, what you know that isn't written down) is exactly what no system holds.

pattern: Workflow the recurring transformations of material you own. Keep manual the judgment calls that happen to recur, and anything that happens once. Never systematize decisions about people.
postscript: If you missed several, look at which kind. Putting judgment calls in 'workflow it' means you'll build something that launders discretion through a template. Putting good transformations in 'keep it manual' means the artisan tax continues for no reason. Both are fixable; that's what the selection rules are for.
